lead.title: Optimized prime editing recreates and stacks disease resistance alleles in tomato
lead.summary: A Plant Cell paper published on 5 November describes three tomato prime editors, TomPE2, TomPE6c and TomPE7, that precisely recreated a pepper resistance deletion in SlBs5 and SlBs5L and raised resistance to Xanthomonas. Stop codons in SlDMR6 gave resistance to both Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas syringae, and a modular system can edit several loci at once. TomPE6c gave the highest share of precise edits. It is peer-reviewed lab and greenhouse work; no field data or yield figures are reported in the abstract.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Two NLR stories stand out: CAR1 prolongs stomatal immunity in Arabidopsis, and Swordholder from Nicotiana tabacum raised field resistance when put into tomato.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: Gap-free soybean genomes, a rice C4 cycle flux demonstration and a peptide that lifts alfalfa transformation efficiency 1.61 times follow the lead.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Seed-applied pydiflumetofen gave 33.6 to 150.4 kg/ha extra soybean yield as cyst nematode pressure rose, but the data are from Ohio, so Prairie relevance is my inference.

plant.title: OsPIL1 trades rice growth and yield against blast resistance via OsINV3
plant.summary: Overexpressing OsPIL1 in japonica cv. LTH restricted growth, cut yield traits and raised blast susceptibility, the opposite of earlier results in indica cv. Acuce, while knockouts resisted Magnaporthe oryzae better. Combined loss of OsPIL1 and OsINV3 helped resistance in LTH but hurt it in Acuce, so genetic background matters. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: Two RNA viruses switch on the 22-nt antiviral silencing pathway in tomato via DCL2b
plant.summary: TMV and tomato bushy stunt virus activate DCL2b through the Dof16 transcription factor and push DCL2b out of the nucleus, which blocks processing of the feedback regulator miR6026. The shift is tied to reduced Tyr69 phosphorylation, and Arabidopsis DCL2 shows the same relocalization. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: Phosphorylation of SGS3 by TOUSLED flips RDR6 between degrading and copying RNA
plant.summary: In Arabidopsis, TOUSLED phosphorylates SGS3 at Ser65 and Ser68, which drives liquid-like siRNA bodies and favours double-stranded RNA synthesis by RDR6. Virus infection instead drives hypo-phosphorylation and solid aggregates, suppressing viral siRNA production. Arabidopsis-only result; abstract only read.

plant.title: The NLR CAR1 extends stomatal closure to block bacterial entry into leaves
plant.summary: Recognition of the conserved type III effector AvrE1 by CAR1, which is enriched in guard cells, prolongs stomatal immunity against Pseudomonas. It also stopped leaf invasion by natural isolates carrying AvrE1. Arabidopsis-based result; abstract only read, no quantitative values in it.

plant.title: Fast-activating NLR Swordholder explains nonhost resistance to an oomycete
plant.summary: Nicotiana tabacum NtSwh has weaker autoinhibition than the N. benthamiana version, so it signals fast enough to outrun effector suppression. Putting NtSwh into tomato raised field resistance to the pathogen with no yield penalty, according to the abstract (no figures given). Peer-reviewed.

plant.title: SlSTP9 and SlDof12 control tomato anther elongation and pollination
plant.summary: CRISPR/Cas9 slstp9 mutants had shortened anthers, premature dehiscence, stigma exsertion and pollination failure, while overexpression raised fruit set. The sugar transporter favours fructose and galactose, and SlDof12 directly represses it. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: GmSTF1/2 activate GmPsbS photoprotection in soybean under high light
plant.summary: CRISPR double mutants of GmPsbS1 and GmPsbS2 showed strong photoinhibition, impaired non-photochemical quenching and more ROS. Overexpressing GmSTF1 improved NPQ and high-light tolerance, with GmGTF3A as a putative co-activator seen in transient assays. Abstract only read.

plant.title: SlCOP1 proteins restrict plastid development in tomato fruit through SlHY5 and GLK2
plant.summary: CRISPR-Cas9 Slcop1 double mutants had enhanced fruit chloroplast development and more carotenoids, while leaves were unaffected, because SlHY5 activates GLK2 in fruit only. Peer-reviewed; abstract only read.

plant.title: FaWRKY7 boosts strawberry fruit resistance to grey mould by repressing FaJAZ4 and FaJAZ8
plant.summary: Transient overexpression raised resistance to Botrytis cinerea and silencing lowered it; the transcription factor binds the FaJAZ4 and FaJAZ8 promoters. Part of the evidence comes from transgenic Arabidopsis, and the effect is only partly dependent on JA-Ile.

plant.title: SiROCX times the cell wall enzyme secretome of the root endophyte Serendipita indica
plant.summary: The transcription factor regulates xylan and cellulose degrading enzymes during colonization of barley roots. Premature activation caused early induction of a host immune marker despite similar fungal biomass, suggesting timing keeps the symbiosis compatible. Mostly in vitro and early stage; abstract only read.

biotech.title: Optimized prime editing recreates and stacks disease resistance alleles in tomato
biotech.summary: Three tomato prime editors (TomPE2, TomPE6c, TomPE7) recreated a pepper resistance deletion in SlBs5 and SlBs5L, raising resistance to Xanthomonas. Stop codons in SlDMR6 gave resistance to both Xanthomonas and Pseudomonas syringae, and TomPE6c gave the highest share of precise edits. A modular multiplex system edits several loci at once. Peer-reviewed lab and greenhouse work; abstract only read.

biotech.title: Gap-free telomere-to-telomere genomes for wild and cultivated soybean
biotech.summary: Complete nuclear, mitochondrial and chloroplast genomes were assembled for Glycine soja SoyW02 and Glycine max Zhonghuang 13. They reveal a conserved subtelomeric exchange hub, refined satellite repeats and diverged duplicated oxidosqualene cyclases. Peer-reviewed; no yield claims.

biotech.title: MsPep1 peptide lifts alfalfa transformation efficiency 1.61 times and enables FTO overexpression gains
biotech.summary: The elicitor peptide shortened the transformation cycle by 20 days. Alfalfa overexpressing FTO, an m6A demethylase, had 24.98% more fresh weight per plant and 10% higher relative feed value in the field, plus better drought and salt tolerance. Peer-reviewed but from one study; abstract only read.

biotech.title: C4 cycle reactions shown to run in transgenic rice
biotech.summary: New transgenic lines and assays detected carboxylation, decarboxylation, Rubisco refixation and regeneration of the C3 donor in rice. The authors cite a possible 50% yield gain from a full C4 pathway, but this is a background estimate, not a result, and a working CO2 concentrating mechanism is not yet achieved.

biotech.title: Atypical PALnc enzymes debottleneck phenylpropanoid production
biotech.summary: A screen of PAL enzymes from 14 plant species found a new clade, PALnc, with feedback activation by p-coumaric acid and other metabolites and higher in planta stability. Stable transgenic Arabidopsis with an Eucalyptus grandis PALnc hyperaccumulated hydroxycinnamate derivatives. Arabidopsis and transient leaf results; abstract only read.

biotech.title: Review: chloroplast genome engineering heads toward commercialization
biotech.summary: Covers the first FDA approval of plant-cell-made biopharmaceuticals for human trials, marker-free edible plants and tools for DNA delivery and expression. Review article, not new data, and the plant-cell drug applications are early stage.

biotech.title: Meta-QTL analysis of eggplant finds 97 stable loci
biotech.summary: Merging 620 QTLs from 23 studies (425 projected onto a consensus map) gave 97 meta-QTLs, narrowing mean confidence intervals from 10.29 to 3.42 cM, and 68 high-confidence candidate genes. Chromosome 6 stands out as a multi-trait hub. Computational meta-analysis, not field validated.

biotech.title: Organelle genomes of the mycoheterotroph Thismia angustimitra show a tiny plastome
biotech.summary: The plastome is only 18,215 bp, and the mitogenome has 22 chromosomes totalling 422,400 bp. No fungal DNA was found, though some intergenic DNA resembles distant angiosperms. Basic genomics with no direct crop application.

biotech.title: Maize lines differ widely in coping with low phosphate and its coupling to nitrogen
biotech.summary: Two dent-pool lines performed poorly under low P and became N deficient, and only they lacked a robust root phosphate starvation response. Inositol pyrophosphates fell in contrasting lines alike, so they appear necessary but not sufficient. Growth-chamber study; abstract only read.

biotech.title: ITS is a multicopy marker for the turfgrass pathogen, so quantification needs single-copy genes
biotech.summary: Digital PCR showed ITS at 33 to 48 copies per genome (34 to 52 with another normalizer) across 27 isolates, while calmodulin, EF1-alpha and MCM7 were single copy. Pathogen species name was missing in the indexed abstract. Diagnostic methods note.

ag.title: Seed-applied pydiflumetofen gains more yield as soybean cyst nematode pressure rises
ag.summary: A network meta-analysis of 21 Ohio trials (787 plots) predicted pydiflumetofen yield gains of 33.6 kg/ha at low pressure to 150.4 kg/ha at high pressure; fluopyram effects were smaller (P = 0.057). Nematode density fell only 4.0 to 12.7% with fluopyram, and not significantly. Peer-reviewed.

ag.title: Korean apple bitter rot fungi carry resistance to thiophanate-methyl and pyraclostrobin
ag.summary: Of 143 Colletotrichum isolates (77 C. fructicola, 66 C. siamense), tebuconazole, fluazinam and iminoctadine worked well. E198A in beta-tubulin and G143A in cytochrome b tracked reduced sensitivity, more often in C. fructicola.

ag.title: Detox genes RsCYP3A24 and RsGSTF5 drive fungicide resistance in Rhizoctonia solani
ag.summary: Under SYP-14288 selection, resistant mutants drifted toward homokaryotic allele fixation and upregulated both genes. Enzyme assays confirmed oxidation by RsCYP3A24 and glutathione conjugation by RsGSTF5. Lab-derived mutants; field relevance not shown.

ag.title: Tea plants defend against Helopeltis theivora with flavonoid chemistry and a repellent volatile
ag.summary: Infestation activated jasmonate signalling and the phenylpropanoid-flavonoid pathway, with pinobanksin-3-acetate a candidate resistance compound. Feeding-induced (E)-beta-ocimene repelled adult males in a dose-dependent way. Lab behavioural work.

ag.title: Whitefly hijacks tobacco NtWRKY6 to switch on a DELLA and stunt growth
ag.summary: Silencing NtWRKY6 restored gibberellin A3 and growth under Bemisia tabaci feeding, and NtWRKY6 directly activates NtRGL2. Tobacco model plant results.

ag.title: Lignin-based boscalid microcapsules release on acid or laccase cues
ag.summary: The 450 nm capsules had 81.6% encapsulation efficiency and 10.4% loading, and the EC50 against Botrytis cinerea at pH 5.0 was 102.50 mg/L, 16% lower than at pH 7.0. They were less toxic to wheat and zebrafish than a commercial formulation. Early-stage lab formulation.

ag.title: Lignosulfonate-based polymer improves saline-alkali soil structure and maize seedlings
ag.summary: At 0.1 wt.% it cut soil column leaching time 29.65%, raised water-stable aggregates 58.15% and cut soluble Na 32.85%. Maize seedling benefits came from a 30-day pot test only, so field results are untested.

ag.title: Sorghum leaf blight incidence and severity map to different genetics in Niger and Senegal
ag.summary: Across 1,339 plot observations and 567,758 SNPs, no marker passed a 10% false discovery rate, and incidence and severity correlated only moderately (r = 0.429). Null genetic result, useful for breeders.

ag.title: Rapid enzyme-mediated assay detects the clubroot pathogen Plasmodiophora brassicae
ag.summary: The assay picked out 157 candidate target regions, used one (Pbspec1), and gave no signal from 12 non-target organisms. Detection limit was in the plasmid copies per microlitre range. Peer-reviewed diagnostic; abstract only read.

ag.title: Mediator subunit Vmg1 is essential for Verticillium wilt pathogenicity
ag.summary: Deleting Vmg1 abolished sporulation, produced malformed microsclerotia and caused no wilt symptoms; the mutant stalled outside xylem vessels. Pathogen species name was missing in the indexed abstract; basic biology, not a control product.

methods: Last issue was 2026-11-05, so the window is 5 to 6 November 2026, using PubMed entry dates; each item date is the publication date in its PubMed record, and two Science Advances items dated 4 November entered PubMed in the window. Web news search found nothing dated in the window (the latest Saskatchewan crop report found was for the week ended 5 October), so no company or news items could be verified and all items come from PubMed abstracts. Source pages were not opened, only abstracts were read. Reviews, Arabidopsis or tobacco-only, lab-stage and null results are flagged, and no company claims were included. Items from earlier briefings were skipped.
